paper.title: A Survey on Large Language Model Based Autonomous Agents

read_sources.note: Used for metadata, authors, abstract, revision history, DOI note, and top-level framing.
Read for construction modules, memory/planning taxonomy, application domains, evaluation strategies, and challenges.
Used to confirm the maintained companion reference repository.

summary.one_sentence: Wang et al. organize LLM-based autonomous agents around profile, memory, planning, and action modules, then survey capability acquisition, applications, evaluation, and challenges.
summary.thesis: The survey's useful move is to treat an autonomous agent as an architecture around the LLM, not the LLM alone: roles, memory stores, plans, tools/actions, and feedback loops shape behavior.
summary.why_it_matters: For agent infrastructure, this is a clear pre-runtime map. Each module implies state management, prompt/schema control, tool execution, evaluation hooks, and failure modes.

prior_state: Traditional autonomous agents were often trained with limited knowledge in isolated environments.
LLMs made open-domain autonomous agents plausible, but early systems were proposed independently with inconsistent terminology.
Research on profiles, memory, planning, tools, and evaluation was fragmented across many agent papers.
The field needed a taxonomy that connected construction choices to applications and evaluation.
problem.key_gap: The survey asks how to systematically summarize LLM-based autonomous agent construction, applications, evaluation strategies, and challenges.
assumptions: LLMs can be central controllers for autonomous agents but need additional modules to operate in dynamic environments.
Agent construction has both architecture design and capability acquisition dimensions.
Applications span social science, natural science, and engineering.
Agent evaluation requires both subjective human-centered measures and objective quantitative benchmarks.

concepts.name: Profile module
concepts.definition: The role/persona component that specifies agent identity, capabilities, relationships, or domain background.

concepts.name: Memory module
concepts.definition: The component that stores perceived information and past behavior so the agent can retrieve, reflect, and act consistently over time.

concepts.name: Planning module
concepts.definition: The component that decomposes tasks, forms plans, and optionally revises plans using feedback from environments, humans, or models.

concepts.name: Action module
concepts.definition: The component that translates agent decisions into specific outputs, tool calls, or embodied/environmental actions.

concepts.name: Capability acquisition
concepts.definition: Strategies for enabling agents to solve tasks, including fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and mechanism engineering.

concepts.name: Subjective and objective evaluation
concepts.definition: The survey's split between human or LLM-judge assessments and quantitative metrics/protocols/benchmarks.

method.core_idea: Survey LLM autonomous agents through three linked taxonomies: construction, applications, and evaluation, with challenges derived from the gaps in those categories.
action_grammar: profile: handcrafted, LLM-generated, or dataset-aligned role description.
memory: short-term context, long-term vector/database/list stores, reading/writing/reflection operations.
planning: single-path, multi-path, external-planner, or feedback-driven planning.
action: output modality, tool/API use, or embodied action.
capability acquisition: fine-tuning, prompt engineering, or mechanism engineering.
application: social science, natural science, or engineering domain.
evaluation: subjective annotation/Turing tests or objective metrics/protocols/benchmarks.
challenge: role-playing, generalized human alignment, prompt robustness, and evaluation limits.
steps: Define the scope around LLM-based autonomous agents rather than general chat models.
Propose a unified construction framework with profile, memory, planning, and action modules.
Survey memory structures, formats, and operations, including short/long-term memory and database-like stores.
Survey planning methods with and without feedback, including external planners and ReAct-style environment feedback.
Survey capability acquisition through fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and mechanism engineering.
Classify applications in social science, natural science, and engineering.
Classify evaluation into subjective and objective strategies and summarize unresolved challenges.
method.pseudocode:
agent = AutonomousAgent(
  profile=role_or_population_profile,
  memory=short_term_context + long_term_store,
  planner=plan_generator(feedback=True),
  action=tool_or_environment_interface
)

agent.capabilities = fine_tuning | prompt_engineering | mechanism_engineering
evaluation = subjective_judgment + objective_benchmark

claims.statement: The survey proposes a unified construction framework with profiling, memory, planning, and action modules.
caveats: The framework is descriptive; individual systems may merge or omit modules.

claims.statement: The profile module can be handcrafted, generated by an LLM, or aligned from real-world datasets.
caveats: Profiles can make simulations easier to build but do not guarantee faithful human behavior.

claims.statement: The memory module is analyzed through structures, formats, and operations such as reading, writing, and reflection.
caveats: The survey summarizes representative formats; actual memory systems can combine multiple formats.

claims.statement: Planning methods are organized into no-feedback strategies, external-planner strategies, and feedback-driven planning from environments, humans, or models.
caveats: The taxonomy predates many 2024-2026 agent planning and verifier systems.

claims.statement: The survey groups LLM-agent applications into social science, natural science, and engineering domains.
caveats: Applications are examples of research directions, not uniformly mature deployments.

claims.statement: Agent evaluation is split into subjective evaluation by humans or proxies and objective evaluation using metrics, protocols, and benchmarks.
caveats: The survey notes weaknesses in both subjective and objective strategies.

claims.statement: The profile-memory-planning-action decomposition is directly usable as a review schema for agent papers because it separates identity, state, control, and effects.
caveats: This is a reviewer inference, but it matches the project's structured-review goal.

evidence.result: The paper's unified framework for autonomous agents is composed of profiling, memory, planning, and action modules.
The survey describes handcrafted profiles, LLM-generated profiles, and dataset-aligned profiles as common ways to specify agent roles.
Memory is discussed through short/long-term structures, formats including natural language, embeddings, databases, and structured lists, and operations including reading, writing, and reflection.
Planning methods include single-path and multi-path reasoning, external planners such as PDDL-based approaches, and feedback-driven planning such as ReAct-style thought-action-observation loops.
The application survey covers social science, natural science, and engineering, including software engineering, robotics/embodied AI, chemistry, and social simulation examples.
The paper distinguishes subjective evaluation, such as human annotation and Turing-test-style comparison, from objective evaluation using quantitative metrics, protocols, and benchmarks.
Profile, memory, planning, and action correspond to identity/configuration, persistent state, control policy, and side-effect surface, which are core schema axes for structured reviews.

agent_infra_takeaways: This survey gives a clean architecture checklist for reviewing agent papers: profile, memory, planning, action, capability acquisition, and evaluation.
Memory formats matter operationally. Natural-language, embedding, database, and structured-list stores expose different retrieval, audit, and mutation semantics.
Planning with feedback is the critical line between static prompt decomposition and real agent control loops.
Profiles should be treated as configuration with provenance, not harmless prompt text, especially in multi-agent simulations.
Evaluation needs subjective and objective signals, but neither is sufficient alone for production-grade confidence.
The construction taxonomy is directly useful for this project's review database because it separates mechanisms that Markdown-only summaries tend to blur.
caveats: The arXiv paper has later revisions; this review preserves the reading-list year while noting the source is actively maintained.
As a survey, it synthesizes primary papers rather than producing new experimental results.
The taxonomy predates many later agent-runtime, safety, and benchmark papers.
The application survey includes early-stage prototypes and research demonstrations, so maturity varies widely.

related_work.note: Xi et al. offer a broader brain-perception-action and agent-society framing; Wang et al. provide a more operational module taxonomy.

related_work.title: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents
related_work.note: CoALA's memory/action/decision decomposition is more formal and cognitive-architecture oriented.

related_work.note: ReAct is a primary example of feedback-driven thought-action-observation planning in the survey.

poc.note: No PoC yet. A useful PoC would be a tiny inspectable agent skeleton with separate profile, memory, planning, and action modules.
